title: Base URL changes re-report errors for invalid speculation rules
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[Respond to base URL changes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#respond-to-base-url-changes) re-parses every `script` whose result is a speculation rules parse result, including ones whose error to rethrow is non-null. [Update speculation rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#update-speculation-rules) then queues another report of the exception, so each `<base>` insertion, removal, or `href` change fires another `error` event at the window.

None of the errors from [parse a speculation rule set string](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/speculative-loading.html#parse-a-speculation-rule-set-string) depend on the base URL (invalid JSON, non-object top level, invalid tag), so the re-parse can only produce the same error. Chromium [doesn't re-parse](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf:third_party/blink/renderer/core/script/script_loader.cc;l=237-246) in this case, and [`speculation-rules/inline-speculation-rules-base-url-errors.tentative.html`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/speculation-rules/inline-speculation-rules-base-url-errors.tentative.html) expects no repeated error.

Maybe respond to base URL changes should skip scripts whose result's error to rethrow is non-null.
